subject: Accessory Dwelling Unit Zoning Regulations
overview: The board received an educational presentation on how new state laws regarding Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) interact with proposed residential zoning districts. The board continued the public hearing on neighborhood and urban residential zoning to May 7 to allow for further research and revisions based on public feedback.

items.title: Neighborhood and Urban Residential Zoning Hearing
items.summary: Continued the public hearing on proposed zoning amendments for neighborhood and urban residential districts to May 7, 2025. The consultant requested additional time to incorporate previous public input and conduct further density analysis.

items.title: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Presentation
items.summary: Innes Associates presented an overview of the new Massachusetts ADU law, explaining the difference between state-protected units and local options the city may regulate. The presentation covered physical typologies, size restrictions, and prohibited regulations such as owner-occupancy and parking requirements in transit-adjacent areas.

items.title: Board Discussion on ADUs and Density
items.summary: Board members discussed how ADUs would function in triple-deckers and multi-family structures, noting that state law triggers 'protected' ADU status wherever single-family homes are permitted. Staff clarified that a City Council subcommittee is currently leaning toward allowing a second ADU by special permit citywide.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Residents requested a 'calculator' or guide to determine if small lots can physically accommodate ADUs and urged the city to provide high-resolution maps and draft language further in advance of meetings. Other comments addressed the impact of ADUs on condo associations and the broader goals of the city's comprehensive plan.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Adjournment
items.summary: Passed over the approval of minutes as none were ready and adjourned the meeting.
